newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bishops join chorus condemning Le Pen.
newsitem.headline: French bishops join chorus condemning Le Pen.

text.p: France's Roman Catholic Church added its moral weight on Tuesday to a chorus of condemnation of far-right National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen for espousing racial inequality, saying it was unacceptable to Christians.

"When a public figure dares to assert the inequality of races as the truth, there is a danger for the whole of society. This assertion undermines the foundations of solidarity which is so necessary in these times of crisis," the Catholic Bishops' Conference said in a statement.
"It fuels racist behaviour, hatred of others and exclusion. It is an attack on the national identity which is based on values accepted by all: liberty, equality and fraternity," it said.
"For a Christian, such statements are unacceptable."

An unrepentant Le Pen stuck to his guns on Tuesday, saying people were equal in law even if they were of unequal ability. While saying France's civilisation is superior, he has carefully avoided saying some races are inferior.

"All men individually have the same rights and dignity, but they are unequal in their ability to understand Greek, or run the 100 metres or swim a kilometre. That's self-evident," the anti-immigration campaigner told Radio Monte Carlo.
"I too am a Christian, and I believe they have a soul."

The hard-right leader said he hoped to attend Pope John Paul's mass in Reims next Sunday celebrating the 1,500th anniversary of the baptism of king Clovis, although the Church said on Monday he had not been invited and would not be admitted to the VIP enclosure.
Le Pen said on Sunday he had been invited as a member of the European Parliament and planned to go to Reims.
